subject: business
intro: Business leads to paid work running and improving organisations — analysing how they operate, finding and developing their people, selling their products and steering their marketing and sales.

roles.title: Management Analysts
roles.what: Conduct organisational studies and evaluations, design systems and procedures, and carry out work-simplification studies — preparing operations and procedures manuals that help management run the organisation more efficiently.
roles.where: The whole syllabus is analyst training: break-even analysis and costs and scale of production from the operations unit, and analysis of accounts from the financial-information unit, are precisely the studies and ratios these analysts perform on companies.

roles.title: Human Resources Specialists
roles.what: Recruit, screen, interview and place people within an organisation, and often handle the wider HR work around them — training, pay and benefits, and employee relations across the business.
roles.where: The People in business unit maps directly onto the job: motivating employees, recruitment, selection and training of employees, and internal and external communication are the processes HR specialists run every day.

roles.title: Marketing Managers
roles.what: Plan and direct marketing policy: measure the demand for a firm's products against competitors, identify potential customers, and develop the pricing, promotion and distribution strategy that reaches them.
roles.where: The Marketing unit — market research methods, the marketing mix and marketing strategy — is the playbook these managers own; the stakeholder-objectives topic frames the demand and competition questions they answer.

roles.title: Sales Managers
roles.what: Plan and coordinate how a product or service actually reaches the customer — setting sales territories, quotas and goals, and directing the distribution and sales teams that hit them.
roles.where: Channels and the marketing-mix element of place from the Marketing unit, plus the business-growth-and-size topics from unit 1, ground the distribution and territory decisions sales managers make.

roles.title: Business Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach business courses at colleges and universities — management, marketing, finance and operations — designing classes and assessments, and often researching and consulting alongside teaching.
roles.where: Every IGCSE unit recurs in their classrooms: from understanding business activity to cash-flow forecasting, income statements and break-even analysis, this syllabus is the foundation their students arrive needing.
